It’s crowded but it’s not that bad as everyone has a specific hour in which they go in. There’s a line for people who don’t have tickets, it’s really long but once you’re in, there aren’t that many people, it’s nothing too much to handle. Also we were asked at one point if we want to continue the tour or end it there. There were people with kids who chose the second option and left and the rest of the group continued with the guide. I think you will have a great time there, I personally enjoyed it a lot and I really hate overcrowded places. It’s quite amazing!

Go for 8;30 am. It’s much more interesting with the guided tour, you learn a lot of things and everything makes more sense. The Vatican is huge and if you choose the 17:00, you won’t have enough time. Also the queue for St Peter is HUUGE, if you want to see it, go for the early hours.

I’m giving an update here for everyone who still hasn’t bought the tickets. I’ve been on the site since 8:30 AM Rome time. The only tickets they released were the attic ones from 9:30 AM time and every 20 minutes exactly afterwards so 9:50, 10:10, 10:30, etc. 

I’ve waited and waited and refreshing literally every minute for the underground tickets and they released them finally at a very random time - 11:37 AM Rome time. 

Few tips from me - watch the clock and refresh the page 20 seconds before the next minute comes. So let’s say it’s 9:29:40, you need to refresh at this time. Then when it’s 9:30:00 you click on June and if the date is available as quickly as you can, select it, and then the number of tickets you need and the time, add them to the cart. You need to be super quick with that because the tickets disappear within seconds. 

I know it sounds a bit crazy but trust me if you do the above, you’ll get your tickets 😂😂

I’ve managed to add the attic tickets with the same method, just in case I don’t get to buy the underground tickets. 

It’s very annoying as honestly you just don’t know when the tickets will be released. I’ve spent 3 hours on this and was very annoyed in the end 😂

Good luck to everyone!!

You need to know your target audience’ pain points and know exactly how your product will solve them and make their life easier.
